title: 96-well Growth Curve Analysis using BEAST in R Studio
author: Norman Van Rhijn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.4fzgtp6
materials: Find the script needed to read your raw data-files. Format the file names like this: plate1-Rep1.txt, plate1-Rep3.txt, plate2-Rep2.txt, plate3-Rep1.txt, plate3-Rep3.txt, plate4-Rep2.txt, plate5-Rep1.txt, plate5-Rep3.txt, plate1-Rep2.txt, plate2-Rep1.txt, plate2-Rep3.txt, plate3-Rep2.txt, plate4-Rep1.txt, plate4-Rep3.txt, plate5-Rep2.txt. Make sure the different replicates are in different files. However, the location in the plate should be exactly the same (i.e., A5 should be A5, B2 should be B2). If this is not the case or replicates are on one plate, transform the original files to match this format. Furthermore, titles of the wells should exactly be the same!
Install BEAST software from CRAN into R studio. Documentation can be found at: https://rdrr.io/cran/beast/man/beast-package.html and https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/beast/beast.pdf.

You can find the script below that you need in order to read your raw data-files, format the file names like this: plate1-Rep1.txt plate1-Rep3.txt plate2-Rep2.txt plate3-Rep1.txt plate3-Rep3.txt plate4-Rep2.txt plate5-Rep1.txt plate5-Rep3.txt plate1-Rep2.txt plate2-Rep1.txt plate2-Rep3.txt plate3-Rep2.txt plate4-Rep1.txt plate4-Rep3.txt plate5-Rep2.txt Make sure the different replicates are in different files. However, the location in the plate should be exactly the same (ie. A5 should be A5, B2 should be B2). If this is not the case or replicates are on one plate, transform the original files to match this format. Furthermore, titles of the wells should exactly be the same!
Install BEAST software from CRAN into R studio. https://rdrr.io/cran/beast/man/beast-package.html Manual can be found: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/beast/beast.pdf

steps.title: Import and format data
steps.instruction: Open R Studio Desktop version 1.1.463, import the file produced by the previous protocol, and run the supplied preprocessing code to create the list `myDataList`. Edit the top two lines of the code to set the desired number of replicates and plates (e.g., set `number_of_plates` to the appropriate integer; the example shows 0). Verify that `length(myDataList)` equals the number of variables/replicates (R) and that each element of `myDataList` is a T × N matrix (time‑points × series). The final object after this step is `myDataList`.

substeps.instruction: Import the data file from the previous protocol.
Run the preprocessing script, adjusting the first two lines to set the correct number of replicates and plates (e.g., `number_of_plates <- 0`).
Check that `length(myDataList) == R` and each `myDataList[[i]]` has dimensions T × N.

steps.title: Load BEAST package
steps.instruction: In the same R session load the BEAST CRAN package with `library('beast')`. If you wish to test the workflow, also load the example dataset using `data("FungalGrowthDataset")`; otherwise skip this line and continue with your own `myDataList`.

substeps.instruction: Optional: `data("FungalGrowthDataset")` to load the example data.

steps.title: Set random seed (optional)
steps.instruction: Set a reproducible random seed, for example `set.seed(1)`, if desired.

steps.title: Run MCMC sampler
steps.instruction: Run the MCMC sampler on `myDataList` using the default number of iterations (`nIter = 70000`) with the command `run_mcmc <- beastRun(myDataList)`. The default settings include a complexity prior parameter `gammaParameter = 2`.

steps.title: Print MCMC results
steps.instruction: Display the MCMC output by executing `print(run_mcmc)`.

steps.title: Plot results to PDF
steps.instruction: Create a PDF file named `beast_plot_fungal_data.pdf` containing the growth‑curve plots by running `plot(run_mcmc, fileName = "beast_plot_fungal_data.pdf", timeScale = 1/6, xlab = "hours", ylab = "growth")`. The PDF will show all curves combined, clustered by change‑points, with individual curves for each isolate.

steps.title: Adjust complexity prior (optional)
steps.instruction: If you want to influence the number of inferred change‑points, modify the `gammaParameter` argument when calling `beastRun`; the default is 2 (smaller values favor more change‑points, larger values favor fewer).
